cohort: 44 women who underwent successful ECV and 88 matched controls who had the same parity and a singleton vertex pregnancy at term, at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal, between 2002 and 2012
finding: Successful external cephalic version (ECV) was not associated with increased rates of intrapartum cesarean delivery or operative vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: The indications for cesarean delivery after successful ECV did not differ between groups; in both groups, cesarean delivery was mainly performed for labor arrest disorders.
